## Spherical cell-to-plain-mean conversion (`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`) {#sec-ch12-centroid}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Default: **off**. Enable with `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1`. The conversion acts on spherical-polar x1 inputs and implies WB even on
Cartesian grids. It inherits the nonzero-gravity three-ghost guard. The five-cell moment solve and six-face pressure
source remove a measure mismatch; neither is a claim of arbitrary-order time integration.
:::

### Derivation

A spherical cell stores $\langle q\rangle_{V^{(1)}_i}=\int r^2q\,\mathrm{d}r/V^{(1)}_i$,
where radius $r$ is in $\mathrm m$ and $V^{(1)}_i=\int r^2\,\mathrm{d}r$ per unit solid angle is in $\mathrm{m^3}$.
The x1 reconstruction instead needs $h^{-1}\int q\,\mathrm{d}r$. Choose a quartic polynomial whose five
$r^2$ cell integrals match five input means, and integrate that polynomial with the plain measure over the target cell.
Linearity gives five weights; requiring equality for degrees zero through four fixes them uniquely.
`x1_plain_mean_stencils` forms and solves those five equations ([`x1_centroid.cpp:104-182`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp#L104-L182)).
For pressure $p$ in Pa, integration by parts gives the radial pressure acceleration density

$$
-\frac1{V^{(1)}_i}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}}r^2\partial_1p\,\mathrm{d}r
=-\frac{\Delta_i[r^2p]}{V^{(1)}_i}+
\frac2{V^{(1)}_i}\int_{r_{i-1/2}}^{r_{i+1/2}}rp\,\mathrm{d}r.
$$ {#eq-ch12-centroid-pressure}

The surface term is the pressure flux. `x1_pressure_source_stencils` integrates the second term from the quintic
through six face pressures ([`x1_centroid.cpp:184-229`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp#L184-L229)). Four-point quadrature integrates the degree-six product exactly.
The polynomial identities are exact; general smooth fields retain interpolation truncation.
`configuration_check.py` verifies the five moments and the integrated pressure identity.
Source derivation: `docs/derivations/x1-centroid-spherical.md@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0` §2–4.

### Numerical method

Five-cell windows move inside the owned region at a clamped wall. Ghost corrections are mirrored, odd for radial
velocity at a reflecting wall; seam ghost rows are replaced by the neighbor's own converted values. The pressure
operator needs six faces, with two neighbor faces beyond a seam. Unusable stencils return the original means.
Only x1 inputs are converted; lateral fluxes retain the original primitives. The spherical pressure operator is also
used for the non-hydrostatic split correction. `balance_column` accepts only Cartesian geometry when XC is on.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch12-centroid-flow
#| fig-cap: 'Spherical conversion: sky-blue circles denote five cell means and orange face markers denote six pressure values $p_{i+1/2}$ in $\mathrm{Pa}$. The two polynomial degrees differ.'
#| fig-alt: "five r-squared cell means; solve moments of degree 0..4; plain means for x1; six faces: pressure source."
#| echo: false
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
XC does not provide a gnomonic measure conversion. XC with face work, radial exact or FC needs new runtime evidence.
Cartesian activation still changes the reference through WB; it is not a universal no-op.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
